analysis.title: GS Bartlett - GS TMT TODAY 10.21.26
key_insights: Futures are higher (Nasdaq +60bps, S&P +25bps, Russell +15bps) alongside global tech strength (KOSPI +3%, Euro tech +140bps). SPCX earnings and an SMCI preannouncement are cited as restoring the AI trade.

SPCX trades +8% premarket after revenue beats in all three operating segments, with outsized momentum in Super Intelligence. Musk said SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to explore a merger.
Read-across from the SPCX print: hyperscalers lower on increased competition (GOOGL -1%, MSFT -50bps, AMZN flat) and semis higher (SMH +2%).
SMCI is up about 12% on its preannouncement, which guided net sales well above consensus. DELL +5% and HPE +4% in sympathy.
NFLX is -7% on a softer Q4 forecast and a FY ad revenue guide cut. AT&T is -4% on Q3 postpaid phone adds that missed consensus.
META, IBM, LRCX, TSLA and TXN report after the close today.
GS Prime reports record tech selling, a sharp reduction in net leverage, Mag 7 net exposure at a new record high, and continued hedge fund performance challenges into October.

Global Info Tech stocks saw the largest 2-week net selling (Oct 5-16) on GS Prime's record (10+ years, -3.3 SDs), driven by both long sales and short sales. Net allocation to Global AI stocks is in the 38th percentile and the group's aggregate long/short ratio is in the 6th percentile vs the past year.

SPCX Q3 revenue and GAAP EBIT beat Street, driven by AI segment revenue (cloud service agreements) and Starlink adoption. Management sees line of sight to 2.5-3GW of nameplate compute by YE26, an incremental 10GW in 2027, and an upside case of more than 20GW by YE27.

SPCX Q1'27 revenue guidance of $33-37bn is well above GSe/Street. Q4'26 capex guidance is above estimates, and GAAP Super Intelligence EBIT missed on elevated stock-based compensation tied to the Cursor acquisition. GS says future funding needs will likely overhang the stock until visibility on capital raises improves.

NFLX Q3 revenue, operating income and GAAP EPS beat guidance and estimates. Q4 revenue, operating income and EPS guide below expectations, FY FCF guide was cut from $12.5bn to ~$12bn on a Q4 real estate transaction, and the FY26 ad revenue guide was cut to ~$2.7bn from ~$3bn on third-party integration delays. Management acknowledged US engagement has room for improvement.

SMCI preannounced F1Q27 revenue of $18.5-19.5bn vs prior guidance of $14.5-15.5bn and GSe/FactSet consensus of about $15.0bn. Gross margin is 12-12.5% vs guidance of 10.4-10.8%. FY27 guidance was not updated (previously $65-72bn). Management said it may need external financing for revenue beyond $80bn. The earnings call is November 3 after the close.
AT&T 3Q postpaid phone net adds were +379k vs consensus +387k. Revenue and EPS were in line, FY26 adjusted EPS outlook was raised, and the capital investment outlook was lowered.

Per Reuters, Samsung and SK Hynix are upgrading their China plants to make more advanced memory chips. They must seek annual US licenses for US-made equipment, and the regulatory limits have contributed to share loss to YMTC.

Macro: 10-year yield 5.123%, 2-year 4.791%, WTI $99.87, gold $4,127.62, VIX 17.41, DXY 101.73. French 10-year yields hit 5% for the first time since 2002. UK September CPI was 3.5% YoY vs 3.4% consensus, an 11-month high driven by motor fuel costs tied to the Middle East conflict.
GS lowers LG Innotek 3Q26 operating profit estimate to W71bn from W247bn on a stronger KRW and weaker optics solution. It cuts the target price to W750,000 from W860,000 and stays Neutral.

GS expects mixed Korean telecom 3Q26 earnings: KT wireless service revenue -3% YoY, SKT revenue +12% YoY with wireless service revenue +22% YoY, LGU+ wireless service revenue +1.5% YoY. GS prefers KT for shareholder return optionality.

GAAP Super Intelligence EBIT below GSe/Street on elevated stock-based compensation tied to the Cursor acquisition. Q1'27 revenue guidance $33-37bn vs GSe/Street estimates (guidance, well above). Q4'26 capex guidance above GSe/Street.

NFLX Q3 reported: revenue, operating income and GAAP EPS above prior guidance and GSe/Street estimates. Q4 revenue, operating income and EPS guided below prior GSe/Street expectations. FY FCF guide cut to ~$12bn from $12.5bn. FY26 ad revenue guide ~$2.7bn vs prior ~$3bn. Q3 buybacks ~$4.8bn vs $4.7bn in Q2, ~$22.3bn authorization remaining.

SMCI F1Q27 preannounced (not yet formally reported): revenue $18.5-19.5bn vs prior guidance $14.5-15.5bn and GSe/FactSet consensus of ~$15.0bn. Gross margin 12-12.5% vs guidance 10.4-10.8%. Prior FY27 revenue guidance $65-72bn, not updated. Earnings call November 3 after the close.
T Q3 reported (first take): postpaid phone net adds +379k vs consensus +387k. Revenue and EPS in line. FY26 adjusted EPS outlook raised, capital investment outlook lowered.
LG Innotek: GS 3Q26 operating profit estimate cut to W71bn from W247bn (estimate, not yet reported).
Korean telcos 3Q26E preview (estimates): KT wireless service revenue -3% YoY, SKT revenue +12% YoY and wireless service revenue +22% YoY, LGU+ wireless service revenue +1.5% YoY.
